q1: SELECT MAX(NUM) AS NUM FROM (SELECT NUM FROM MYNUMBERS GROUP BY NUM HAVING COUNT(NUM) = 1) AS T
q2: SELECT IF(COUNT(*) =1, NUM, NULL) AS NUM FROM MYNUMBERS GROUP BY NUM ORDER BY COUNT(*), NUM DESC LIMIT 1
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT MAX(NUM) AS NUM FROM (SELECT NUM FROM MYNUMBERS GROUP BY NUM HAVING COUNT(NUM) = 1) AS T
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT IF(COUNT(*) =1, NUM, NULL) AS NUM FROM MYNUMBERS GROUP BY NUM ORDER BY COUNT(*), NUM DESC LIMIT 1
explanation: Q1 finds the maximum number from the set of unique numbers in MYNUMBERS. Q2 groups by NUM, orders by count ascending and NUM descending, and returns one row. Q2 can return a non-unique number if multiple rows share the same count but different NUM values. Q1 strictly returns the max of unique numbers.
